# Typedef-impact feasibility — issue #251

The public corpus supports selecting a development candidate through independent static references; it does **not** yet supply a verified typedef-impact key.
Only this session report was written; no benchmark/product files were changed and no commit was made.

Counts: [sources](../benchmark/sources.json) records **9 loose `.ctl` files in actor-framework**, commit `371c631c16155d88f02be11a953e4964d7452fd8`, and **0 in pylavi**, commit `35d2a0318f71dcb87bb9c431dc00700ee6b9fb75`; read-only `git ls-files` enumeration independently matched both counts.
All nine have recorded LVSR `20008000` (`20.0.0f0`). [Coverage](../benchmark/coverage.json) additionally inventories **7 `.ctl` members** in `actor-framework/Builds/actor_framework_2024_for_2020-2.0.0.23.vip`: 16 loose/member occurrences altogether, not 16 independent typedefs.
Coverage records only `20.0.0f0` across fields for five loose controls; four loose controls and all seven package members also contain `vers` values `20018007` (`20.0.1f7`). These conflicting version fields do not establish authoritative native save-version semantics; no native version check ran.

Method: scan 471 tracked actor-framework `.vi`, `.vim`, `.lvproj`, `.lvlib` and `.lvclass` files for exact ASCII basenames, then parse matching XML `Item` attributes. Five candidates were inspected; three are documented below. Paths are relative to `$LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT/actor-framework/`; `@N` denotes a zero-based original binary byte offset. Listed binary hits are name-reference evidence, not confirmed instances. Archive consumers were not scanned.

| Candidate `.ctl` | XML declaration evidence | VI binary name-reference evidence: exact paths and offsets |
|---|---|---|
| `Core/ActorFramework/Message Dequeuer/Dequeue Priority.ctl` | `Core/ActorFramework/Message Dequeuer/Message Dequeuer.lvclass`: `Item[@Name='Dequeue Priority.ctl']`, `Type='VI'`, `URL='../Dequeue Priority.ctl'` | `Core/ActorFramework/Message Dequeuer/Dequeue.vi` @2449,2484 |
| `Core/ActorFramework/Message Priority Queue/DVR Contents.ctl` | `Core/ActorFramework/Message Priority Queue/Message Priority Queue.lvclass`: `Item[@Name='DVR Contents.ctl']`, `Type='VI'`, `URL='../DVR Contents.ctl'` | `Core/ActorFramework/Message Priority Queue/Dequeue Timed Out.vi` @2025,2056,12987; `Core/ActorFramework/Message Priority Queue/Flush.vi` @9431; `Core/ActorFramework/Message Priority Queue/Obtain Priority Queue.vi` @4205,4236,10115; `Core/ActorFramework/Message Priority Queue/Priority Dequeue.vi` @15531; `Core/ActorFramework/Message Priority Queue/Priority Enqueue.vi` @11259; `Core/ActorFramework/Message Priority Queue/Release Priority Queue.vi` @7975 |
| `Core/ActorFramework/Time-Delayed Send Message/Time-Delay Override Options.ctl` | `Core/ActorFramework/Actor Framework.lvlib`: `Item[@Name='Time-Delay Override Options.ctl']`, `URL='../Time-Delayed Send Message/Time-Delay Override Options.ctl'`; `Providers/AFPP 2024 for 2020.lvproj`: same item name, `URL='/<vilib>/ActorFramework/Time-Delayed Send Message/Time-Delay Override Options.ctl'`; both `Type='VI'` | `Core/ActorFramework/Time-Delayed Send Message/Time-Delayed Send Message Core.vi` @2337,2382; `Core/ActorFramework/Time-Delayed Send Message/Time-Delayed Send Message.vi` @1941,1986,6289,6334; `Core/ActorFramework/tracing/Support/TDM Registry.vi` @301,374,2321,2394,5177,5250; `Core/ActorFramework/tracing/Trace Generation/Generate Trace for New Time Delayed Message.vi` @2193,2266; `Core/ActorFramework/tracing/Trace Generation/Generate Trace for Skipped Time-Delayed Message.vi` @2233,2306; `Core/ActorFramework/tracing/Trace Generation/Generate Trace for Stopped Time-Delayed Message.vi` @2213,2286 |

XML establishes declarations only: URL resolution and installed `<vilib>` identity were not verified. Binary strings may represent cached/linkage information; neither their presence nor absence establishes complete consumer coverage.
Static work here cannot confirm that a `.ctl` is a typedef rather than a custom control, its strictness/type/defaults, VI-internal typedef instances and object locations, transitive users, dynamic references, or which consumers change/break after an edit.
A usable key additionally needs preserved and hashed before/after revisions, a precise authorized edit recipe on derived copies, native typedef/consumer properties and diagram locators, resolved dependencies and environment versions, affected and unaffected controls, discriminating behavior/error observations, and independent checking as required by the [protocol](../benchmark/protocol.md#oracle).
Verification: `python3 -I policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check` exited **0**, with 49 indexed evidence references and no errors/missing entries; this verifies the evidence index only. `benchmark_executed=false`, `benchmark_ready=false`, `tool_quality=null` remain explicit.

## What next
Policymaker can order a bounded native feasibility inspection beginning with `Dequeue Priority.ctl` and its one statically identified VI, before commissioning a controlled-edit development case. This report completes the static measurement; native work remains unexecuted.
Resume from the pinned inventories and exact offsets above; do not repeat startup reads or whole-inventory dumps, infer instance coverage from strings, or treat package occurrences as independent cases. The existing headless environment forbids source authoring/editing, so a paired-revision experiment also requires an authorized development environment or suitably supplied revisions.

No changes to merge.
